top5.literature: Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial Machine Learning (Wiley 2018) ch.4 (average uniqueness u_i=mean_t(1/c_t), sample weighting w_i=u_i) + ch.3 (meta-labeling). MQL5 'Machine Learning Blueprint Part 4: Label Concurrency' (mql5.com/en/articles/19850, AFML ch.4 replication): uniqueness-only weighting +6.7% F1 / +7.5% accuracy, BUT return-attribution weighting COLLAPSED both (F1->0) — the direct warning against blending uniqueness x |return|. top5.title: Make llm_eval answer the only question that justifies the LLM spend: incremental-over-pred (partial-Spearman controlling for ML pred), not raw Spearman
top5.gap: llm_eval journals the ML pred alongside each conviction score s and carries it into the sample tuples, but the keep/kill verdict is computed on RAW correlation of s vs realized only — pred is DEAD. VERIFIED: pred captured at llm_eval.py:139 and appended at :151 (samples.append((s, realized, pred))), but the entire compute block uses only s_vals/realized: rho = _spearman(s_vals, realized) at :178 drives report['spearman_s_vs_return'] and the printed keep/kill verdict at :193-198. The 3rd tuple element is never read. CRITICALLY the prompt SHOWS the LLM the ML pred (llm_analyst.py:456-457), so a high Spearman can be the LLM merely ECHOING the ML signal (redundant) and a low one can hide real orthogonal alpha. The verdict that gates a real decision is confounded by the very signal the LLM is meant to complement: s drives llm_mult=0.5+s sizing (base_loop.py:1649, applied :1313, 0.65-1.5x) AND forced liquidation on consecutive s<0.15 vetoes, at ~$7/mo. llm_eval imports cleanly on the Mac (confirmed) so the estimator is genuinely mac_now-testable; no tests/test_llm_eval.py exists today.
top5.roi_case: The ONLY candidate on priority axis #3, which the user explicitly wants ('make the LLM EARN its place with a measurable lift'), and it is the single highest-leverage fix to the LLM-value question: it converts llm_eval from a metric that CANNOT distinguish complementarity from redundancy into one that answers the binary $7/mo keep/kill AND is the PREREQUISITE measurement for the deferred model-facing LLM sizing items (conf-field fix, llm_mult attribution) — those can only be validated once incremental lift is measurable. measurement_safe (offline, zero live-signal change) so it ships directly; ~1 file of pure numpy + 1 new test file, fully Mac-buildable (scipy.stats + statsmodels both import here). Beat a 4th financial-soundness pick for the #5 slot on PORTFOLIO grounds: it is the only item covering priority axis #3, and skipping it would leave the LLM's value formally unanswerable while three #2 items pile up.
top5.implementation: MAC_NOW (measurement_safe, ships directly): refactor run_eval to SPLIT API-bound sample collection from a pure compute_incremental_report(samples) over (s, realized, pred) triples so the statistics are unit-testable WITHOUT Alpaca. Report THREE things side-by-side: (1) PRIMARY = partial Spearman rho(s,realized|pred) via rank-residualization (rank-transform all three, closed-form 2-var OLS residualize rank(s) and rank(realized) on rank(pred), Spearman the residuals) — the gap between RAW and PARTIAL IS the echo diagnostic; (2) the 2x2 agree/disagree grid {LLM-bull s>=0.5, LLM-bear} x {ML-bull pred>0, ML-bear} with explicit per-cell n (off-diagonal disagreement cells are where the LLM can ONLY be adding orthogonal value); (3) OPTIONAL/SECONDARY encompassing regression realized = a + b1*pred + b2*z_s with Newey-West variance at lag=forward_bars-1 and an HLN n-1 t-dist p-value — this self-reports significance and is the honest verdict driver. tests/test_llm_eval.py (pure numpy, fixed seed, N~2000): redundancy (s=sigmoid(pred) -> raw HIGH, partial ~0, b2 NOT significant — catches the echo the current metric can't); orthogonal-alpha (realized=a*pred+b*g+noise, s=sigmoid(g), g _|_ pred -> partial recovers positive b even when raw ~0 — proves the flip case); null; 2x2 disagreement-cell edge; degeneracy (constant pred -> pred_degenerate flag, no crash); statsmodels ORACLE cross-check (b2 / partial-rho to 1e-6); plus a SMALL-n power caveat assertion (at N=40 the verdict ABSTAINS). JETSON_LATER (measurement_safe, no promotion gate): run python llm_eval.py --days 30 (and --asset crypto/stock) on real journals carrying the pred field; one-time statsmodels correctness audit on the full stack.
top5.literature: Harvey, Leybourne & Newbold (1998, JBES 16(2):254-259) 'Tests for forecast encompassing' — regression e^A_t=lambda(f^B_t-f^A_t)+u_t, H0:lambda=0 (A encompasses B => B adds nothing), small-sample t(n-1) correction + HAC/Newey-West for overlapping h-step horizons (exactly our forward_bars=24 case). PResiduals::partial_Spearman (CRAN) — partial Spearman = Spearman of residuals after regressing rank(X) and rank(Y) on control rank(Z); the RankIC-with-control analogue of the standard quant Information Coefficient, scale-free and robust to the LLM's monotone-nonlinear 0-1 mapping and fat-tailed returns. Chen, Kelly & Xiu, 'Expected Returns and Large Language Models' (SSRN 4416687) — finds LLM news signals contain information INCREMENTAL beyond traditional technical predictors and firm characteristics: the field measures LLM value as incremental-over-baseline, precisely the metric llm_eval is missing.
top5.risk: Refinement of an existing offline tool, not a live defect — zero live-signal change. The honest hazard (folded in from refutes): at realistic journal volume (often n~30-80, thinned by forward-horizon-elapsed and per-asset splits) a partial-rho of 0.03-0.15 is statistically indistinguishable from zero (null std ~0.15-0.19 at n=30-50), so the verdict must gate on the SIGNIFICANCE of b2 with CIs, NOT a bright-line rho_partial>0.03; raise the n guard to >=60-100 and emit 'insufficient_power'/'pred_degenerate' flags rather than a confident flip. The 2x2 disagreement cells are the LEAST populated (the LLM is shown the pred and rarely disagrees) — report n and don't lean on thin cells. Frame the payoff as diagnosing echo-vs-orthogonal + a significance-tested incremental coefficient, NOT a promised clean keep/kill flip. Real numbers need Jetson journals carrying pred (only recently started being written) — expect thin n initially.

top5.title: Persist account-level _peak_equity so the drawdown de-leveraging ladder survives restarts (today it silently disables on every restart-mid-drawdown)
top5.gap: self._peak_equity initializes to a HARDCODED 100_000 (VERIFIED base_loop.py:98) and is only updated IN-MEMORY from acct.equity (VERIFIED :535-536). _save_position_state persists hwm/trailing/last_trade/daily_trades but NOT _peak_equity (VERIFIED the data dict at :304-310 has exactly those four keys; grep confirms peak_equity appears ONLY at 98/535/536/1270/1271). The drawdown ladder computes dd=(_peak_equity-_equity)/_peak_equity and cuts size 25/50/75% at 10/15/20% DD (VERIFIED :1270-1277). So after ANY restart mid-drawdown from a peak>100k, _peak_equity resets to max(100k, current)~current, dd snaps to ~0, and the entire de-leveraging ladder turns OFF precisely when the account is underwater. On an 8GB Jetson Orin Nano, restarts on retrain/OOM/power events are ROUTINE, not rare, so the window is hit in normal operation.
top5.roi_case: Serves BOTH the #1 (Jetson restart resilience) and #2 (financial soundness) priority axes — the only candidate touching the top axis with real ROI (the rank-1 scaler-slice that nominally hits #1 is a microsecond no-op). Surgical, ~6 LOC + 1 test, no deps/perf/memory cost, fail-direction safe. Without it a bot restarted at a 15% drawdown sizes at 1.0x instead of 0.50x (2x the intended risk; 4x at 20% DD), exactly when de-risking matters most. Beat the scaler-slice decisively (a real risk-control fidelity gap on the single most consequential downside-control mechanism vs a microsecond cleanup) and earned the slot over a 4th #2 item by ALSO covering priority axis #1, giving the portfolio breadth.
top5.implementation: MAC_NOW (buildable+testable now, but NOT via importing base_loop — VERIFIED `import base_loop` fails with ModuleNotFoundError: joblib via predict_now, so the naive 'instantiate the loop' test does NOT run here): extract the persistence round-trip and the dd-ladder arithmetic (the math at base_loop.py:1270-1277) into pure free functions and unit-test THOSE with numpy/json + a synthetic state file. top5.title: Slice the seq_len window BEFORE scaler.transform in get_live_prediction (bit-identical partially-dead-code elimination)
top5.gap: In get_live_prediction(), current_features = df[feature_cols].values is the ENTIRE post-dropna fetched window (predict_now.py:312), scaler_X.transform(current_features) transforms ALL of them (:318), and then only the last seq_len rows are used: sequence = current_features_scaled[-seq_len:] (:319). VERIFIED: current_features_scaled has exactly two occurrences (318 define, 319 sole consumer), so it is dead beyond the slice; scaler_X is a joblib-loaded RobustScaler whose transform is strictly elementwise per-column ((X-center)/scale), so transform(current_features[-seq_len:]) is bit-identical to transform(current_features)[-seq_len:]; the upstream len(df)>=seq_len guard makes the slice always valid. Transforming the discarded leading rows is pure waste, repeated per symbol per ~30s cycle across both 24/7 crypto and stock books. Batch paths (backtest.py:97, hypersearch:508) build sliding windows over ALL rows and legitimately need the full transform — left untouched.
top5.roi_case: Hits priority axis #1 (Jetson perf) and is the rare ZERO-functional-risk item (row-independent transform => bit-identical output), so it ships directly measurement_safe with no gate, and it is fully provable on the Mac NOW with a synthetic numpy RobustScaler equivalence test. Cuts the live-path transform input by ~2-4x fewer rows (effective post-dropna window ~74-100 -> seq_len 8-40) and drops the oversized intermediate, per symbol per cycle. It earns the #5 slot over a 4th financial-soundness pick to keep the portfolio honest about priority axis #1 being the user's #1 stated priority AND because it is the highest-confidence lowest-effort item on the board (a verified one-line change + one test). It is explicitly ranked LAST because, post-verification, the absolute saving is small (single-digit microseconds/cycle on a sub-microsecond-scale operand) and it does NOT touch the real perf lever.
top5.implementation: MAC_NOW (measurement_safe, ships directly): replace predict_now.py:318-319 with a single line `sequence = scaler_X.transform(current_features[-seq_len:])` (drop the dead current_features_scaled intermediate). tests/test_scaler_slice_equiv.py (pure numpy synthetic RobustScaler): assert np.array_equal(transform(window)[-seq_len:], transform(window[-seq_len:])) across shapes; assert the reshape/tensor-input path is identical; an ast guard that current_features_scaled is gone (dead-intermediate eliminated). Leave backtest.py:97 and hypersearch_v2.py:508 untouched (batch paths need all rows). JETSON_LATER (measurement_safe): one-time bit-identical regression of predicted_return/lstm/lgb/q10 on real symbols + a transform/cycle microbenchmark (RSS+CPU) under TORCH_NUM_THREADS=2 to confirm no behavior change.
top5.literature: RobustScaler row-independent transform arithmetic (scikit-learn preprocessing docs: each row is (x-center)/scale elementwise). Partially-dead-code elimination / loop-invariant code motion (compiler optimization: hoist/eliminate computation whose result is discarded). Sliding-window preprocessing latency scaling (edge-AI narrowing of the preprocessing window) — cited honestly as the analogy, NOT as a literal multiplier, since here preprocessing does not dominate the cycle.
top5.risk: Effectively zero functional risk (bit-identical output, verified). The honest hazard is OVERSELLING the ROI (both refute critiques flagged this): the real saving is single-digit microseconds/cycle and a ~36KB transient freed at function return regardless — it does NOT relieve 8GB Jetson MEMORY pressure and moves the perf needle ~0% because the cycle is dominated by network fetch, the full-window feature computation (indicators.py rolling(252)/(231) recomputed over the WHOLE window every 30s cycle — the ACTUAL perf lever this does NOT touch), the torch LSTM forward, and two LightGBM boosters. Ship it as a correct zero-risk cleanup, claim NO measurable latency/RSS win, and flag the full-window rolling-recompute as the real perf item for a future wave.

Three financial-soundness items (#2) anchor the wave because that axis has the highest-confidence, best-evidenced, lowest-overfit-risk gaps right now — and crucially they are ORTHOGONAL, not redundant: rank 1 fixes TRAINING honesty (the loss over-counts non-IID overlapping labels), rank 2 fixes SELECTION honesty (the gate is a single 12% holdout with no overfit-probability), and rank 4 fixes RISK-CONTROL honesty (the drawdown ladder silently disables on restart). Rank 4 doubles as the only real win on priority axis #1 (Jetson restart resilience), and rank 5 is the pure-#1 perf item kept for axis coverage but ranked last and explicitly de-hyped after verification proved it a microsecond no-op (its refutes were decisive on magnitude).
